title: PostgreSQL internals, Part 2: MVCC and row versions
tldr: How PostgreSQL lets readers and writers run together: every UPDATE writes a new row version stamped with xmin and xmax, transaction IDs and the pg_xact commit log, snapshots (xmin:xmax:xip_list) and the visibility rule, Read Committed vs Repeatable Read snapshot timing. Then inspecting versions live, timeouts that keep transactions short, how one old snapshot bloats every table, hint bits that make reads write, the subtransaction cache limit, and how PostgreSQL's MVCC compares with InnoDB's.
